verses.zh: 耶和华啊，荣耀不要归与我们，不要归与我们；要因你的慈爱和诚实归在你的名下！
verses.en: Not to us, O Lord, not to us,but to your name bring honor,[NOTE:1] for the sake of your loyal love and faithfulness.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 115. The psalmist affirms that Israel’s God is superior to pagan idols and urges Israel to place their confidence in him.
verses.commentary:
115:1-8 This strophe is about the futility of idolatry! There is only one God (cf. Jer. 10:6-10; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM)! There
is only one hope for "the nations." All Bible students have presuppositions about the "meta-narrative" of the Bible (i.e., its basic
purpose or message). YHWH's desire for the nations to trust Him is mine (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).

115:1 What a powerful verse. Glory (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY [doxa])
belongs to YHWH alone, not any human agency or group. This is because

- of YHWH's lovingkindness (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS [hesed])

- of YHWH's faithfulness (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT; also see

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD [OT])

- YHWH is sovereign, Ps. 115:3 (cf. Ps. 103:19; 135:5-6)

- YHWH hears and acts but idols cannot, Ps. 115:4-7 (cf. Ps. 135:15-18; Deut. 4:28; Isa. 44:12-17; Jer. 10:3-5)

- YHWH is the creator, "maker of heaven and earth" (cf. Ps. 115:15b,16; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN)

▣ "Your name" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH.

verses.zh: 为何容外邦人说：他们的　神在哪里呢？
verses.en: Why should the nations say,“Where is their God?”
verses.commentary:
115:2 The question of line 2 is the theological issue. Israel was to be a kingdom of priests (cf. Exod. 19:5-6) to
help the world know and understand YHWH. But because of her faithlessness the world saw only the judgment of God (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36).

The very question of line 2 is repeated in Ps. 42:3; 79:10 (cf. Joel 2:17; Micah 7:10).

verses.zh: 然而，我们的　神在天上，都随自己的意旨行事。
verses.en: Our God is in heaven.He does whatever he pleases.[NOTE:1]
notes: The psalmist asks the Lord to demonstrate his loyal love and faithfulness, not simply so Israel may benefit, but primarily so that the Lord will receive honor among the nations, who will recognize, contrary to their present view (see v. 2), that Israel’s God is committed to his people.
verses.commentary: 115:3 This focuses on the sovereignty of YHWH (cf. Ps. 135:6; Dan. 4:35).

verses.zh: 他们的偶像是金的，银的，是人手所造的，
verses.en: Their[NOTE:1] idols are made of silver and gold—they are man-made.[NOTE:2]
notes: He does whatever he pleases. Such sovereignty is characteristic of kings (see Eccl 8:3).
The referent of the pronominal suffix is “the nations” (v. 2).
verses.commentary:
115:4 "silver and gold" These are the precious metals that overlaid the images made from stone
or wood (cf. Deut. 4:28; 28:36; 29:17).

▣ "The work of man's hands" Here is the problem (cf. 2 Kgs. 19:18; Isa. 44:9-20; Acts 17:29).

verses.zh: 有口却不能言，有眼却不能看，
verses.en: They have mouths, but cannot speak;eyes, but cannot see;
verses.commentary:
115:5-7 Idols are human productions. They are personified by the nations who made them,
but they cannot see, move, hear, speak, or act! YHWH is the God who acts!

115:7b Because Ps. 115:5 mentions "speech," this may refer to some type of divination done in
the name of the pagan idol. See notes at Deut. 18:10-11 online.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION

verses.zh: 有耳却不能听，有鼻却不能闻，
verses.en: ears, but cannot hear;noses, but cannot smell;

verses.zh: 有手却不能摸，有脚却不能走，有喉咙也不能出声。
verses.en: hands, but cannot touch;feet, but cannot walk.They cannot even clear their throats.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the work of the hands of man.”

verses.zh: 造他的要和他一样；凡靠他的也要如此。
verses.en: Those who make them will end up[NOTE:1] like them,as will everyone who trusts in them.
notes: Heb “they cannot mutter in their throats.” Verse 5a refers to speaking, v. 7c to inarticulate sounds made in the throat (see M. Dahood, Psalms [AB], 3:140-41).

verses.zh: 以色列啊，你要倚靠耶和华！他是你的帮助和你的盾牌。
verses.en: O Israel, trust in the Lord.He is their deliverer[NOTE:1] and protector.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “will be.” Another option is to take the prefixed verbal form as a prayer, “may those who make them end up like them.” sn Because the idols are lifeless, they cannot help their worshipers in times of crisis. Consequently the worshipers end up as dead as the gods in which they trust.
verses.commentary:
115:9-15 Notice the threefold designation and command ("trust," BDB 105, KB 120, Qal
IMPERATIVE).

- O Israel, trust YHWH, Ps. 115:9,12 (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL [the name])

- O house of Aaron, trust YHWH, Ps. 115:10,12 (i.e., Levitical priests; see (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVITICAL PRIESTS)

- You who fear/revere YHWH, trust Him, Ps. 115:11,12 (this could be a further characterization of #1 and 2,
cf. Ps. 135:19-20, or a reference to non-Israelites, cf. 1 Kgs. 8:41-43; Ezra 6:21; Neh. 10:28; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN)

In turn YHWH will be

- their help (cf. Ps. 18:2; 33:20; 70:5; 121:2; 124:8; 146:5)

- their shield (cf. Ps. 28:7; 59:11; 84:9,11; 119:114; 144:2)

- mindful of us (cf. Ps. 98:3)

- bless both great and small

- give you and your children increase (BDB 414, KB 418, lit. "add," Hiphil JUSSIVE, cf. Ps. 112:2)

There are consequences in time (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28) and eternity for idolatry! There
are consequences for personal faith and faithfulness in YHWH (cf. Ps. 115:16-18)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

verses.zh: 亚伦家啊，你们要倚靠耶和华！他是你们的帮助和你们的盾牌。
verses.en: O family[NOTE:1] of Aaron, trust in the Lord.He is their deliverer[NOTE:2] and protector.[NOTE:3]

verses.zh: 你们敬畏耶和华的，要倚靠耶和华！他是你们的帮助和你们的盾牌。
verses.en: You loyal followers of the Lord,[NOTE:1] trust in the Lord.He is their deliverer[NOTE:2] and protector.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “[you] fearers of the Lord.” See Ps 15:4.

verses.zh: 耶和华向来眷念我们；他还要赐福给我们：要赐福给以色列的家，赐福给亚伦的家。
verses.en: The Lord takes notice of us;[NOTE:1] he will bless[NOTE:2]—he will bless the family[NOTE:3] of Israel,he will bless the family of Aaron.
notes: Another option is to translate the prefixed form of the verb “bless” in vv. 12-13 as a jussive, “may he bless” (see v. 14).

verses.zh: 凡敬畏耶和华的，无论大小，主必赐福给他。
verses.en: He will bless his loyal followers,[NOTE:1] both young and old.[NOTE:2]

verses.zh: 愿耶和华叫你们和你们的子孙日见加增。
verses.en: May he increase your numbers,yours and your children’s.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the small along with the great.” The translation assumes that “small” and “great” here refer to age (see 2 Chr 15:13). Another option is to translate “both the insignificant and the prominent” (see Job 3:19; cf. NEB “high and low alike”).

verses.zh: 你们蒙了造天地之耶和华的福！
verses.en: May you be blessed by the Lord,the Creator[NOTE:1] of heaven and earth.
notes: Heb “may he add to you, to you and your sons.” The prefixed verbal form is jussive, indicating this is a prayer.

verses.zh: 天，是耶和华的天；地，他却给了世人。
verses.en: The heavens belong to the Lord,[NOTE:1] but the earth he has given to mankind.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the heavens [are] heavens to the Lord.”

verses.zh: 死人不能赞美耶和华；下到寂静中的也都不能。
verses.en: The dead do not praise the Lord,nor do any of those who descend into the silence of death.[NOTE:1]
verses.commentary:
115:17 "The dead" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

verses.zh: 但我们要称颂耶和华，从今时直到永远。你们要赞美耶和华！
verses.en: But we will praise the Lordnow and forevermore.Praise the Lord!
verses.commentary:
115:18 God's people will forever bless (Piel IMPERFECT) and praise (Piel
IMPERATIVE) YHWH. This implies an afterlife separate from the idolatrous who "do not praise"
and "go down into silence" (cf. Ps. 6:5; 30:9; 88:10-11; 94:17).

▣ "forever" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

▣ "Praise the Lord" As with Ps. 113:9c, the LXX moves
this to the beginning of the next Psalm.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Explain the OT terms

- lovingkindness

- faithfulness/truth

- Why are both Ps. 115:1 and 2 so theologically significant?

- How is YHWH different from pagan idols?

- Does Ps. 115:9-11 refer to one group, two groups, or three groups?

- List the things YHWH is and does for faithful followers.

- Explain Ps. 115:16 in your own words.

- Explain "go down into silence" of Ps. 115:17b.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This Psalm is about the utter futility of trusting in manmade idols. Only the One true Creator/Redeemer Deity
is worthy of trust.

- This Psalm is characterized by repeated phrases.

- "not to us," repeated twice, Ps. 115:1

- "they have. . .," seven IMPERFECTS, Ps. 115:5-7

- "trust," four (three IMPERATIVES and one PARTICIPLE; the ancient
versions such as LXX, Peshitta, and Vulgate, interpret this MT IMPERATIVE as a
PERFECT), Ps. 115:8-11

- "He will bless...," six (five Piel IMPERFECTS and one Qal
PASSIVE PARTICIPLE), Ps. 115:12-15,18

- "praise the Lord"

- negated, Ps. 115:17 (Piel IMPERFECT)

- commanded, Ps. 115:18 (Piel IMPERATIVE)

- Psalm 114 and 115 are combined in

- the Septuagint

- the Aleppo Hebrew MS of the 10th century

- the Leningrad MS of the 11th century (the basis of the MT)
